records.title: Does the A-03 image audit bound missed doubled runes?
records.question: Does the source's preserved image-count audit satisfy its declared controls and justify K≤26 missed doublets?
records.summary: The published counts and arithmetic reproduce, but the source misses its image agreement gate and its arithmetic-only planted control does not measure image detection. The observed excess of 26 pairs is not an upper bound on hidden merges.
records.finding: The classifier reports 99.4146% agreement against a 99.5% gate. Its source code loads 13,381 component rows but does not process them in the K control. The saved counts give 108−82=26 excess image pairs and a stated threshold of 93 additional pairs; without a measured error bound, the first number cannot cap the latter.

scope.representation: Pinned Dukotah Round10 classifier output, log and Round16/A-03 source receipt, not original image pixels.
scope.procedure: Hash-check six source files, parse classifier agreement and count log, recompute the source threshold and arithmetic K control, inspect whether source code actually reprocesses glyph rows, and give a finite nonnegative error assignment with the same observed surplus.
scope.parameters: Source image agreement gate 99.5%; source comparison floor 1.38%; source counts as preserved at f08b20b.
scope.exclusions: No fresh image transcription, no measured classifier error rate for merged glyphs, no general autokey exclusion.

records.limitations: This is an audit of saved source receipts and inference, not an independent reading of the source images or a test of every autokey variant. A constructed error assignment shows logical possibility, not empirical plausibility.

records.title: Alberti branch proposal: LP2-39 row and modulo-31 arithmetic
records.question: Do the source's identified LP2-39 row, 4–5–4 shift sums and claimed modulo-31 matches reproduce as written?
records.summary: The 19-rune row and four signed short-group sums reproduce. Standard modulo 31 turns the right totals −33 and −39 into 29 and 23, rather than the claimed positive 2 and 8; the proposed disk reading remains untested.
records.finding: The identified row has 19 runes in groups of 3, 4, 6, 5 and 1. Left raw short sums −13 and −17 and right raw short sums −33 and −39 reproduce. The right pair reduces modulo 31 to 29 and 23, not the source's +2 and +8; obtaining the positive pair requires an additional direction reversal. The proposed deciphering rule cannot be checked from these arithmetic inputs.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-39 UTF-8 rune transcription and the source's two explicit 13-number plant arrays, short overlay and posted final arrays, copied into a fixed plan. Source transcript identified by SHA-256, not republished.
scope.procedure: Recount the source-identified row's rune groups; calculate the two four-element overlaid short sums and all posted 4–5–4 final-array sums; reduce the signed values using standard nonnegative modulo-31 residues. Repeat short sums at all 13 cyclic starts for each plant array as a sensitivity diagnostic.
scope.parameters: One LP2-39 row; two posted 13-number arrays; one posted four-number overlay; fixed groups 4, 5, 4; 13 starting positions for each array; modulus 31. No fitted key, symbol mapping or selected plaintext.
scope.exclusions: Complete Alberti disk alphabets, rule-state transitions, branch inheritance, letter assembly, word-selection search, full-page reading, or a chance probability for the source's selected interpretation. The separate method files and diagrams referred to in the discussion are not available as pinned inputs here.

records.limitations: The transcript states the arrays but does not supply a complete fixed disk configuration and transition table. Its group and target choices were made during an evolving exploration, so the 13-rotation check is sensitivity analysis, not a statistical null. It cannot validate or refute the purported LP2-39 plaintext.

records.summary: Neither F-clock rule recovered a declared twelve-rune opening in 55 LP2 pages.
records.finding: Neither rule revealed a known opening. Pausing just the key or both clocks was tested with both known keys, every starting phase, and both arithmetic directions.

scope.representation: First twelve GP29 runes, including headings, of LP2-00–55; omit runeless LP2-50. Page-local state. Other characters do not advance it.
scope.procedure: Alternate ordinary/reversed cipher alphabets, each with its own known repeating key. Decode F normally but hold the selected key position there. Compare always-toggling versus F-paused alphabet clocks; compare each head with nine fixed twelve-rune known-reading openings.
scope.parameters: 2 key assignments × 104 phase pairs × 2 first alphabets × 2 signs × 2 clock policies = 1,664 settings; 55 pages; 823,680 exact comparisons. 1,664 roundtrips on 87 prescribed runes plus 1,664 forced-marker controls.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, cipher alphabet permutations, literal/removed F, other interruption runes, word resets, additional layers, noninitial starts and unknown plaintext openings. No historical exact-method replay is claimed.

records.title: B-04 cryptographic seed streams against fixed LP2 openings
records.question: Do the published B-04 cryptographic seed keystreams produce a fixed known-reading opening on any included LP2 page under the source key-skip rule?
records.summary: Across 1,385,600 source-defined keystream configurations, none can produce any of nine fixed 12-rune known-reading openings at the start of one of 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages under the stated key-skip rule.
records.finding: The longest structurally feasible opening is six runes; zero of 1,385,600 configurations match all 12 runes. This is a new fixed-crib test of source-defined candidates, separate from the source English-score sweep.

scope.representation: Current Liberpedia GP29 rune transcription; the first 12 runes of every nonempty LP2-00–55 page, read separately. Nine fixed 12-rune openings from published reading CSVs.
scope.procedure: Regenerate the pinned source seed bytes through 16 source generators and five reductions. For every forward/reverse stream, sign and ciphertext-Atbash setting, exactly test whether any key-skip path can produce a fixed opening; no English score or beam pruning.
scope.parameters: 2,165 seeds × 16 generators × 5 reductions × two directions × two signs × two Atbash states = 1,385,600 configurations; zero offset; at most three rejected draws per emitted rune; all 55 nonempty LP2 page starts; nine fixed 12-rune cribs.
scope.exclusions: No different seeds or hashes, nonzero offsets, independent page keys, word resets, alternative transcriptions, other plaintexts or original source English-scoring claims.

records.limitations: It assumes one of nine known-reading 12-rune openings begins at one of 55 nonempty page starts. It tests zero key offset, the source B-04 keystream candidates and skip bound; it does not test other plaintexts, word resets, altered transcriptions, new seeds, or a general decryption mechanism.

records.title: LP2 doublets at proposed block boundaries
records.question: Do the 86 adjacent repeats collect at block boundaries for sizes five, seven or thirteen, or at any selected periodic offset?
records.summary: For page-anchored sizes 5, 7 and 13 the boundary counts are 18, 13 and 6, close to conditional expectations. The best of 434 size/phase placements is ordinary under the same search on fixed-count controls.
records.finding: The 86 adjacent repeats do not gather unusually at the boundaries of five-, seven- or thirteen-rune blocks. Searching 434 combinations of block size and starting offset also found no stronger pattern than the shuffled comparisons commonly produced.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 transcription, filtered to 29 alphabet runes separately within each page.
scope.procedure: Mark adjacent equal-rune edges; count phase-zero hits for block sizes 5, 7 and 13; search every size 2–29 and shared phase; compare the maximum standardized excess with 3,000 per-page fixed-event-count randomizations.
scope.parameters: 86 event edges among 12,901 edges; page-start clock; 434 size/phase configurations; 3,000 seeded controls.
scope.exclusions: Page-specific unknown phases, variable block sizes, interruptions, changed transcription, low total doublet count, and a complete block-cipher decoder.

records.limitations: The control conditions on each page’s observed doublet count and tests placement only. It does not rule out blocks with separately chosen page phases, interrupted clocks, or another cause of the low total.

scope.representation: Source-derived English GP29 plaintext, correct generator streams, planted ciphertext and decoded rune paths; no manuscript candidate.

records.title: LP2-15–22: digit spirals and Roman/HALFMAN selector
records.question: Do the reported digit-grid contacts and seven-number Roman/HALFMAN result reproduce from archived rune text, and what happens under nearby orientation and window choices?
records.summary: The 17×17 and 59×59 GP-digit grids, the registered rune-boundary counts, and the selected Roman total of 225 reproduce. Two of 80 local orientation/window cases meet both 225 and descending order, but both reuse the same seven numbers. No rune-to-plaintext rule is supplied.
records.finding: LP2-15 body has 150 runes and 289 GP digits; LP2-16–22 has 1,744 runes and 3,481 GP digits. Under the specified registration, alternating rune-boundary contacts match 12/16 and 16/16. Transposed labels 5–11 give LXLLLXV, rearranged as LLLLXXV by direct HALFMAN ranking; symbol values sum to 225. Exactly 2/80 local orientation-window trials also meet sum 225 and descending order, but both contain the identical seven panel values.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-15 body runes with nine-rune header excluded, plus all LP2-16–22 runes; each GP prime expanded to ordinary decimal digits. The printed LP2-15 number panel is an independent fixed input for the Roman selector.
scope.procedure: Build center-out right–down–left–up 17² and 59² digit spirals; register the printed 4×4 labels through 1→2, 2→3, 3→N−1, 4→N; check odd-label starts and even-label ends. Transpose the printed panel, take labels 5–11, convert final two digits to Roman numeral first symbols and apply direct HALFMAN ranking. Enumerate eight symmetries and ten consecutive seven-label windows as nearby controls.
scope.parameters: 17×17 and 59×59 streams; sixteen contacts per grid; direct rank order 4,1,5,3,6,2,7; Roman symbols I,V,X,L; target symbol-value sum 225 and descending values. The 80-case scan does not include other word readings, numeric extractions, registrations or permutations.
scope.exclusions: No independent derivation of the five candidate plaintext words; no cipher execution, held-out plaintext, calibrated chance probability or claim that the supplied grids are authorial instructions.

records.limitations: The representation, source grouping, proposed words, Roman extraction and coordinate map were chosen during exploration. Contacts sharing a rune are dependent. The 80 nearby choices are not the full search space and cannot be read as a p-value. Matching arithmetic does not identify a cipher or decrypt any text.

records.summary: Recounts eleven supplied LP2 section groups under four rune-to-number representations and compares square lengths across every contiguous page interval from LP2-00 to LP2-39.

The LP2-15 17×17 case requires excluding its header; the proposed 54×54 and 15×67 cases require additional, unverified selections.

records.summary: Fresh dot measurements at three thresholds and exact rational bounds exclude shared ordered radii at native scale. Page-specific radii and rescaling remain outside the test.
records.finding: No, under this construction. Circles centered on the three horizontal dots cannot all meet at a point inside each page when the same radius is assigned to the corresponding dot on both pages.

scope.representation: Original 2400x3600 JPEGs; four-connected grayscale components; exact pixel-centroid fractions.
scope.procedure: Measure three ordered horizontal dots per page at three thresholds; derive exact residual corner bounds and compare with the lower bound imposed by shared radii.
scope.parameters: Thresholds 100,140,180; explicit crop boxes; area>200; 0.7<width/height<1.3; fill>0.6. Targets inside [0,2399]x[0,3599]. Same radii at A,B,C across pages.
scope.exclusions: Rescaling; page-dependent radii; reassigned radius order; outside-page targets; different dots; pairwise intersections; compass stepping; rune selection and plaintext.

records.limitations: Fixed measured centers and native pixel scale; no rescaling, radius reassignment, outside-page targets or pairwise/stepping constructions. Threshold checks are not a full uncertainty interval. Human review pending.

records.title: What a crib fixes in a feedback table
records.question: How many arbitrary 29-entry feedback substitution tables remain compatible with each fixed 12-rune opening at an LP2 page start?
records.summary: A handful of proposed openings are internally consistent with arbitrary feedback tables, but each leaves at least 18 of the 29 table entries free.
records.finding: Ciphertext feedback gives 31 consistent page-opening pairs out of 495, each with 18 or 19 free entries. Plaintext feedback gives one consistent pair out of 495, with 20 free entries. The consistent cases determine at most five of the next twelve ciphertext-feedback positions or one sequential plaintext-feedback position; none is a validated reading.

scope.representation: First 24 recognized GP29 runes including headings from each of 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages.
scope.procedure: For each fixed 12-rune opening, infer f(previous ciphertext) or f(previous plaintext) from C_i−P_i modulo29 at i=1..11. Reject conflicting assignments, count 29^(29−r) full extensions for r assigned inputs, and measure coverage on the next twelve ciphertext positions without a truth label.
scope.parameters: 2 feedback modes × 55 page starts × 9 fixed openings = 990 partial-table inferences; 11 constraints per proposed opening; 29 possible input slots.
scope.exclusions: First-rune primer inference, unknown plaintext and continuations, language scoring, alternate alphabet orders, later positions, changing tables, and other cipher layers.

records.limitations: A compatible partial table is not evidence of a true decryption. The first rune needs an external primer, future plaintext is unknown, and only the fixed page starts, proposed openings and two feedback states are covered.

records.title: LP2-00–02: audit the 729 ÷ rune-index proposal
records.question: Does the posted 729 divided by GP-index rule reproduce its worked first word and specify a complete output on the 729-rune section?
records.summary: The 729-rune count is correct, but the worked example uses index 28 for prime 107, which has zero-based index 27. F makes division undefined at 34 positions; line clock and wrap choices change hundreds more outputs.
records.finding: All three pages contain 729 runes, but the claimed first-word index for prime 107 is 28 rather than its canonical zero-based 27. Literal arithmetic with the archived rune gives Y rather than the report's AE at that position. The 34 F runes have index zero and no quotient. Without wrapping, 335 of 695 non-F outputs fall outside the alphabet under global line counting; global and page-reset wrapped outputs differ at 396 of 695 positions.

scope.representation: Every archived rune of LP2-00–02 in printed line order, GP prime values and zero-based 29-rune indices. The source's eight first-word indices are fixed in the plan, including its 28 for prime 107.
scope.procedure: Verify the 729-rune count, then for every nonzero index j calculate floor(729/j), remainder, base index modulo 29, and the posted fractional threshold with both global and page-reset line counts. Keep both raw and wrapped candidate indices; mark zero-index F undefined. Compare the first eight source indices and labels with the claimed worked example.
scope.parameters: Three pages, 33 source rune rows, exact rational fractional comparisons, line numbering from one, no word rearrangement or removal. Modulo-29 wrapping is an explicitly additional convention for comparison, not a source claim.
scope.exclusions: A fixed rule for F; chosen neighboring letters; letter rearrangement or dummy-word removal; image-level review of every rune; a full plaintext or a statistical language claim; other 729-based constructions.

records.limitations: The supplied post names no complete F handling, wrap rule, global-versus-page line clock or deterministic selection from its neighboring letters. Its excerpted image is unavailable; this audit identifies the post by hash and uses the archived transcription. The chosen full-stream conventions are declared extensions and do not recreate all manual postprocessing in the discussion. Human review pending.

records.title: Two LP2 transcriptions: word-boundary sensitivity
records.question: Do any of the 33 non-rune differences between preserved seventh-onion and wiki texts on LP2-00–55 change the published joined-page rune-token positions or lengths?
records.summary: No. Both 12,956-rune streams yield the same 2,896 token starts and complete length histogram. Each of the 33 cross-source gap substitutions also leaves the token starts unchanged under the declared parser.
records.finding: All 33 one-gap substitutions and the complete alternate transcription preserve every one of the 2,896 token-start positions, the full length histogram, the 109 tokens of length ten or more, and the single 11–11–10 window. The ordered 12,956-rune stream is identical.

scope.representation: Preserved combined seventh-onion LP2-00–55 rune text, 56 wiki page text files, and the stored 29-rune alphabet. Ordered rune streams are identical; non-rune gaps may differ.
scope.procedure: Split combined text at its 55 percent-mark page separators. Remove slash/CR/LF wraps, concatenate pages, and apply the published rune-token parser with optional internal apostrophes. Compare complete source versus wiki and swap each of 33 differing gaps into the wiki text individually. Compare exact token-start rune ordinals and length metrics.
scope.parameters: 56 pages in numeric order; headings retained; 33 one-gap variants; rune-token starts zero-based; no image-driven correction or tuned punctuation rule.
scope.exclusions: LP2-56–57 and their three additional gap differences; punctuation-sensitive key resets, printed-number consumption, alphanumeric-grid bytes, visual adjudication, and any claim that the two texts are interchangeable for all methods.

records.limitations: This is exact agreement under one parser, not an image audit or a test of all boundary-sensitive ciphers. Different punctuation and number-grid content can matter when a method explicitly uses those marks. records.finding: The solved substitution gate passes 178/178; dense source-segment physical-splice recovery passes 189/189 against its 50% gate. scope.representation: All 58 byte-matched LP2 JPEGs, source-canonical line context, pinned fresh 229-class image bank and the original T2 control scripts. Source segments 45–54 are manuscript pages 45–49 and 51–55.
scope.procedure: Verify source and image hashes; use pinned fresh T2 line map/probe; run unchanged source physical-splice plants and enforce its dense recovery gate; run original indel plants, scoring and component-count labels; run positional separator detector and 19-row shortlist. scope.parameters: Source seeds 3301 for 200 requested splice positions per stratum and 1337 for one missing plus one extra rune plant per line; source glyph-fit filter, zero indel-flag threshold calibrated from solved pages, source separator width rules.
scope.exclusions: Historical NPZ byte replay, blind transcription, multi-error power, manual pixel adjudication, the unimplemented C4 deleted-separator plant and any unconditional bound on true error count.

records.limitations: The 229-class bank is a fresh instrument, not the unavailable historical 226-class array. Splice placements exclude 29.5% of proposed glyph-width pairs. records.summary: The 28-bin chi-square is 42.056 (69/2,000 conditional draws at least as high); it restates the earlier difference IoC. Adjacent nonzero differences match 432/12,676 times, inside the conditional 412--492 range. Neither statistic identifies the cipher.
records.finding: The histogram imbalance is near the upper end of the conditional reference, but it is algebraically the same information as the previous difference IoC at fixed zero count. The new order-sensitive adjacent-equality count is inside its reference range.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00--55 rune indices and their successive within-page modular differences; original zero positions retained.
scope.procedure: Count all 28 nonzero difference residues and adjacent equal nonzero differences; compare both with a zero-mask-preserving independent-uniform reference.
scope.parameters: Modulus 29; residues 1--28; lag-one adjacent nonzero differences only; 2,000 simulations with seed 33012026; no chosen page or bin subset.
scope.exclusions: Plaintext or key recovery, structured and nonuniform keys, cross-page transitions, other lags, alternate rune mappings, image transcription and selection-adjusted inference.

records.limitations: Model and diagnostics were chosen after the doublet and difference-IoC observations. records.title: 2012 P.S. digit-block layout readings
records.question: Do the fixed column and line readings of the 2012 P.S. digit block reveal printable pair-ASCII text or a pinned longer constant?
records.summary: Six bare-block and four indented-layout readings of the original 131 digits all fail the calibrated text-shape and pinned-constant screens. Two four-digit motifs appear only in separate indented routes.
records.finding: No reading reaches 95% printable digit-pair ASCII or contains a pinned longer constant. The bare block has no 3301 or 1033 motif; the five-column indented variant places one in each of two different routes. Ten planted messages pass; 200 random blocks produce no hits at the amended gate.

scope.representation: The three original backslash-continued P.S. digit lines (40+45+46=131 digits) from the pinned 2012 signed-message text; second variant preserves the five-column visual indent of P.S. and a following space.
scope.procedure: Read bare lines in four column directions, concatenation and reversal; repeat four column directions with a five-column indent on the first line. For each, test both two-digit pair alignments for printable ASCII fraction >=95%, longer pinned constants and report-only short motifs/compositeness.
scope.parameters: Six bare and four indented readings; two pair alignments; ten planted readable blocks; 200 random 131-digit three-line controls. The source raised its initial 80% cutoff to 95% after the negative control failed and before real-data screening.
scope.exclusions: Arbitrary column widths, digit substitutions/reordering, other encodings, running keys, additional source messages and any interpretation of a four-digit motif alone as a hit.

records.limitations: This is a fixed-layout test, not a proof that the historical message contains no other hidden content. The five-column visual-indent extension was disclosed after the bare-block negative. Short four-digit motifs were report-only and do not establish a decoded message.

records.title: Can missing duplicate runes hide an autokey pattern?
records.question: Can twenty missed adjacent duplicate runes restore the nonzero difference-diagonal unevenness predicted by one ciphertext-autokey rule?
records.summary: For exact adjacent duplicate insertions, all 28 nonzero rune-difference counts are unchanged. Even an artificial 20-count allowance reaches CV 0.066 against the source's 0.40 signal bar.
records.finding: The pinned transcription yields 9,640 within-word pairs, 60 doublets and nonzero difference CV 0.0608. Physical duplicate restoration leaves that CV invariant for any number of insertions. An exact upper bound allowing 20 freely allocated nonzero-diagonal additions is 0.0656; at 40 it is 0.0717. A separate checker confirms every count and the insertion identity for all 29^3 three-rune contexts.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty '%' segments of the pinned krisyotam_runes.txt, matching source LP2-00–54 labels; within-word adjacent rune indices modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Compute nonzero difference-diagonal counts and CV; insert exact adjacent duplicates algebraically and via exhaustive three-rune contexts. Give an artificial adversary k=0..40 arbitrary additions to the 28 nonzero counts and compute its exact maximal CV. Plant a separate synthetic lumpy ciphertext-autokey versus uniform control.
scope.parameters: 9,640 adjacent pairs, 60 doublets; 28 nonzero diagonals; k=0..40, with the source decision at k=20; CV signal bar 0.40, safe bar 0.30.
scope.exclusions: Source Pride & Prejudice-based control numbers, source surrogate null distribution, plaintext-autokey variants, other feedback equations, off-diagonal transcription errors, and plaintext distributions that are nearly uniform.

records.limitations: This bounds only exact adjacent-duplicate deletion/restoration and the specified ciphertext-autokey difference statistic. The pinned source omits pride.txt, so its English-corpus planted-control numbers and surrogate null are not exactly replayed; a declared synthetic lumpy control passes instead. The source amended its chi-square clause after its first run; the physical invariance does not depend on that clause. Other feedback rules, correlated multi-rune errors and nearly flat plaintext distributions remain outside scope.

records.title: Does the missing-doublet pattern resemble a lag-one filter?
records.question: Does the unsolved LP2 stream distinguish a continuous lag-one repeat filter from tested recency, rebalancing and line-reset controls calibrated to the same repeat rate?
records.summary: The 86 residual adjacent repeats match a continuous lag-one-only filter better than the tested recency/rebalancing or line-reset controls. The comparison cannot distinguish computer code from a person applying the identical rule to otherwise machine-like symbols.
records.finding: Independent input measurements reproduce the 86/12,955 lag-one repeat rate, 3.488% lag-2–8 equality, 0.936 window-58 chi-square per degree of freedom, and 4/86 line-crossing repeats. In the source's 200-replicate matched-control ladder, models with extra recent-symbol avoidance or window rebalancing are distinguishable and rejected; the line-reset model is also distinguishable and rejected. The no-extra-effect hand rung has combined discrimination power 0.110 and remains unresolved.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited LP2 segments of pinned UTF-8 rune transcription, concatenated in page order; slash and page markers retained for line-scope comparisons. 12,956 runes, 55 pages, 594 nonempty physical lines, 648 occupied source line ordinals.
scope.procedure: Independently parse raw runes and reproduce lag equalities, repeat gaps, window chi-square, line-crossing doublets and page dispersion. Freshly run the pinned source fingerprint/controls script with 200 replicates, all controls calibrated to the manuscript lag-one repeat rate, and verify its gate, powered model ladder and scope test.
scope.parameters: 29-rune alphabet; lags 1–8; windows 29/58/116/290; 200 source replicates per modeled family; six hand-model rungs plus uniform, continuous filter and line-reset controls; acceptance interval central 95%; minimum discriminator power 0.80.
scope.exclusions: Other transcription layers, alternative human or machine generators not in the source ladder, an exact cipher/key, the physical identity of the author or pad entropy source.

records.limitations: This is a bounded comparison among specified generators, not proof of a literal machine implementation or entropy source. Controls are calibrated to the observed adjacent-repeat rate. The model ladder does not cover every human strategy; a continuous hand-applied lag-one rule on machine-like symbols is observationally equivalent here. The source counts 648 occupied slash/page line ordinals, whereas the text contains 594 nonempty physical lines.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune indices from LP2-00–55; 2,901 solved plaintext runes for conditional frequency/position calibration. Nine LP2 section boundaries prevent a false adjacent pair.

scope.exclusions: Other text layers, alternate word segmentation, changing marker runes, zero or adaptive multipliers, unequal or shared homophones, stateful alphabets, non-LP1 plaintext priors and additional cipher stages.

Old source page labels actually select LP2-01–38; the source-defined but uncalled Fibonacci stream and unfinished Berlekamp–Massey reconstruction are excluded. Other generator lengths, feedback clocks and page ranges remain open.

records.title: Do the proposed two-time-pad regions match?
records.question: Do the six fixed aligned-copy regions in three pinned Wulfic legacy scripts exist on their verified LP2 input, and what does the separate page-pair difference screen show?
records.summary: The three scripts’ specific identical-span premises fail on their committed source pages; a separate page-pair frequency screen does not establish key reuse.
records.finding: The corrected source stream has 8,226 runes. Five of six proposed paired regions exceed it; the sole in-bounds region matches at 7/404 aligned positions and differs at the first. The P27/P44 prefix also fails. The independent 1,122-case page-pair screen reaches IoC 1.2296 at most; 43/199 page-shuffled full searches reach at least that maximum. Only 2/10 matched-length planted known-reading pairs encrypted with a shared key cross the source 1.15 threshold.

scope.representation: Corrected source old page_21–54 = LP2-04–37, GP29 rune-only, continuous 8,226-rune stream. Label-disambiguation check on LP2-27 and LP2-44. Four direct-reading LP1 pages provide matched-length planted pairs.
scope.procedure: Check all six source asserted identical regions, the claimed page27/page44 prefix and period bounds on the original committed Git page objects; replay the separate all-page-pair ±IoC source function, then 199 whole-search page-wise shuffles and all ten fixed 137-rune shared-key plants.
scope.parameters: Six asserted regions, one 6,726-rune period, 34 pages, 561 unordered pairs ×2 operations=1,122 screens, IoC>1.15, 199 seeded full-search shuffles (seed20261023), five 137-rune reading windows forming ten fixed pairs.
scope.exclusions: Unknown key-reuse alignments or periods, arbitrary key clocks, crib readability scoring under the failed source-copy assumption, alternative transcriptions, and separate solved/reference-text running-key branches.

records.limitations: This falsifies six named identical-ciphertext premises, not general shared-key encryption: equal keys can yield different ciphertexts when plaintexts differ, and equal ciphertext alone does not prove equal keys. All 34 source page blobs exist in Git despite the sparse local checkout and match the site pages; the source pair-score functions were replayed exactly. The period and crib loops based on the failed alignments are not meaningful complete decoding tests. The page-pair controls were added after preliminary outcomes were viewed. Page shuffling preserves unigram counts, not natural plaintext, and the IoC screen misses most planted reuse pairs at length 137. Running-key branches of one source script are separate from this grouped claim.
